prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t honestly name one single “best” lawyer for every truck accident — the right attorney depends on the specifics of your case (severity of injuries, who was at fault, whether the trucker was a commercial carrier, etc.). Instead, here’s a practical way to find the best personal injury attorney in Dallas for a truck-accident case and how to choose among strong candidates.

What you should look for
- Trucking-specific experience: look for attorneys who regularly handle commercial truck/crash cases and know FMCSA rules, logbooks, electronic control module (ECM) data, maintenance records, and common trucking-defendant tactics.  
- Trial experience: many carriers push quick settlements; a lawyer who will and can take a case to trial is usually stronger leverage.  
- Resources and network: trucking cases often need accident reconstruction, ECM/black-box analysis, vocational experts, life-care planners, etc. Make sure the firm can pay for these up front.  
- Track record: verdicts/settlements in truck cases, peer recognition (Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, AV Preeminent from Martindale-Hubbell), and client reviews.  
- Communication and accessibility: clear point of contact, timely responses, and a clear plan.  
- Fee structure: most personal injury lawyers work contingency (no fee unless you recover). Confirm percentage, costs, and when costs are deducted.

Where to search and verify credentials
- Texas State Bar (to confirm license and disciplinary history).  
- Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell for ratings and peer reviews.  
- Local Dallas resources: Dallas Bar Association, Texas Trial Lawyers Association.  
- Google/Avvo and client reviews (read multiple).  
- Ask for recent trucking-case results and references.

Questions to ask in a free consultation
- How many truck accident cases have you handled? How many in Dallas/Fort Worth?  
- Have you handled cases against large trucking companies or national carriers?  
- What were examples of cases you’ve won or settled (outcomes, injury types)?  
- Who would handle my case day-to-day? Will you take it to trial if needed?  
- What experts would you hire for my case and who pays up front?  
- What is your fee percentage and how are costs handled?  
- How long do you estimate until resolution?  
- How will you communicate case status and how often?

Immediate steps you should take now (if you haven’t already)
- Seek/continue medical care and keep all records.  
- Preserve evidence: photos, dashcam/phone footage, truck license plate, company name, driver info, police report.  
- Don’t give a recorded statement to the trucker’s insurer without an attorney.  
- Gather witness contact info.  
- Note the truck’s DOT number or carrier name (if known); that helps identify the company.

How I can help
- If you want, tell me a few details (where in Dallas the crash occurred, your injury severity, whether the truck was commercial, whether you’ve already talked to any lawyers), and I’ll suggest how to prioritize firms or draft a short message you can use to contact attorneys for a consultation.  

If you prefer, I can also provide a short template with the exact questions to ask a lawyer at an initial consult. Which would you like?
